title: Wayfinder: University schedule engine (C# + CP-SAT)
description:
## Destination

A validated, implementation-ready spec for an automated university timetable engine (C#, same solution as ScheduleLib): builder API over the existing domain, constraint model (hard requirements + weighted preferences) solved with OR-Tools CP-SAT, room model with curs/lab room types and override rules, and an input pipeline seeding the model from the existing hand-written (parsed) schedule while keeping lesson composition exactly. Validation = user sign-off of the spec plus a small real-data prototype proving the solver converges (prototype on a throwaway branch, not the main line).

## Notes

- C#, new projects inside the ScheduleLib solution; reuse the existing domain model (CONTEXT.md: Group / SubGroup / Specialization / alternatives).
- Solver: OR-Tools CP-SAT (decided at charting). Requirements = hard constraints; preferences = weighted objective terms.
- Only day/timeslot/room are variable; lesson composition (course, teacher, group partition, weekly count) is kept exactly.
- Room model (Room rules semantics, resolved): no kinds — each Room = Building + Number + OptionalFloor with approximate SeatCount + ComputerCount (catalog on the builder; stub seeds: big-three lecture ≈80, mid ≈50, small ≈40, labs ≈24 seats/≈20 computers); hard rules seats ≥ attendance (derived from the group partition, overridable) and computers ≥ computer-need (lab-type defaults to attendance; overrides per course/teacher/group, each as requirement or preference); pins are scoped and deliberate (negate rules, never questioned), overlapping pins error unless DeliberateOverride on the more specific; ____ is the placeholder room (never solver-assigned, its lessons schedule normally); PE/online have no room; the parser owns the configurable remap/alias table (2Anexă≡2a; 326/6→326/4 fixed in source data). Largeness emerges from capacity, not kind. Room features (flags) participate in requirements — known flags: VR headsets, 3D printer, air conditioning, interactive whiteboard, regular whiteboard; 423/4 carries the VR gear (user, 2026-09-06).
- Split lessons (specializations / optionals / language partitions) must co-time: same day-of-week + slot after assembly.
- Speed over determinism (user, 2026-09): multi-worker solves, wall-clock budgets fine. No agent/LLM inside the engine.
- Wayfinder rules: one decision per session; HITL grilling tickets are launched by the user in separate chats; research/context-gathering may run alongside. Prototypes live in their own worktrees/branches and are throwaway. Research findings land in docs/wayfinder/ + resolution comments on their tickets.
- Group-structure data received and interpreted: docs/wayfinder/group-structure-2026-2027.md (+ raw xlsx under docs/wayfinder/inputs/2026-2027/). Schedulable unit = (course, language) section merging students across academic groups/programs, split into lab subgroups ~13-21; optional-course blocs run in parallel.

## Decisions so far

- [Charting session]: destination = validated spec (+ throwaway prototypes), not the implementation; migrations, agent integration, packaging, full-data runs out of scope.
- [Charting session]: solver = off-the-shelf CP solver; OR-Tools CP-SAT picked (hard/soft native, C# nuget).
- [Charting session]: variable axes = day x slot x room only; composition and teachers fixed.
- [Charting session]: room model = curs/lab typing inferred from schedules, default + override rules; capacities stubbed.
- [Charting session]: engine lives in new projects inside the ScheduleLib solution.
- [DJ gap, user answer]: "DJ" = Dezvoltarea Jocurilor; both a specialty (program) and a specialization legitimately carry the name — typed references only, no regex/string matching (detail in docs/wayfinder/group-structure-2026-2027.md §4).
- [Research: CP-SAT viability](ScheduleLib-6xo.8, closed; docs/wayfinder/research/cpsat-viability.md): Google.OrTools 9.15.6755 (net8.0, linux-x64 satellite) runs on the .NET 11 preview SDK; faculty-scale model (~5e4 literals) solves in seconds-to-minutes; no incremental interface — rebuild + hint; Timefold (no .NET) and custom DFS confirmed out.
- [Grilling: Constraint model & scoring](ScheduleLib-6xo.2, closed; full resolution on the ticket): Requirement vs Preference two-tier taxonomy fixed (incl. student day-load 6 hard/5 soft, PE-last soft, parity splits with parity-set model); weighted sum, no lexicographic hierarchy; structural constraints auto-added (externality = prototype experiment); nudge interface dropped (hints instead); determinism dropped (speed first); weights live at builder level, classes are weight-agnostic; defaults seeded by mining research (6xo.11).

  • [Research: Room inventory & curs/lab inference](ScheduleLib-6xo.9, closed; docs/wayfinder/research/room-inventory.md): 65 room strings ≈ 59 real rooms across 2024–2027 schedules (no pre-2024 data in repo): ~21 computer labs, ~17 lecture rooms (113/4, 213a/4, 404/4 + off-site Mediacor absorb ~90% of weekly curs), ~15 seminar-side rooms, 2 dual-use; (lab) records land in lab rooms ~97%, (sem) never in labs; Limba străină/română computer-less, Psihologie labs are requirement-exceptions only (historically ran inside ordinary computer labs); names encode no capacity — stubs stay demand-side; open questions (capacities, suffix semantics, room-attribute vs lesson-requirement, 415/4 and 239/4/254/4 classification, typo normalization, null-room lessons) feed the Room rules grilling.
  • [Research: Parsing pipeline recon](ScheduleLib-6xo.10, closed; docs/wayfinder/research/parsing-pipeline-recon.md): pipeline = data/<year>_sem<N>/{zi,fr} discovery + MD5-cached parse → ScheduleLoader components → ScheduleBuilder.Build() (unify names, validate, classify subgroup labels, assign implicit splits, validate overlaps) → immutable Schedule (scoped DI) → PDF/website/Excel/Calendar outputs; composition lives on LessonData (LessonGroups ≤16, Teachers[], RoomId bare string, single SubGroup/Specialization/Alternative, Parity on WeeklyLessonDate); splits are separate lessons, ImplicitSplitConfig duplicates per (spec, alt), parallel alternatives = allowlisted overlaps, no bloc entity; seeding seam candidates: A) consume built Schedule directly like the PDF task (recommended to evaluate), B) flattened seed projection; gaps: string rooms w/o capacity, derived weekly counts, section-level lab subgroups outside the model, positional ids.

  • [Research: Mine current schedules for implicit rules](ScheduleLib-6xo.11, closed; docs/wayfinder/research/implicit-rules.md): ranked defaults from 5 semesters (~6,800 entries): gapless group days (81–94%, pref w≈8), day-load ≤5 slots (confirms 6-hard/5-soft), parity splits real (17–24% of entries), late slots + Saturday = upper-year electives, group/teacher no-overlap confirmed; CONTRADICTS the 6xo.2 PE-last soft default (only 14–60%; PE pattern is room=null, Tue/Thu 93%, never slots 5–6) — user call pending in spec assembly; negatives: curs-morning/lab-afternoon, same-course-same-slot, lunch structure.
- [Grilling: Room rules semantics](ScheduleLib-6xo.3, closed; full resolution on the ticket): requirement-driven room model — no kinds; Room = Building+Number+OptionalFloor with approximate Seat/ComputerCount; hard rules seats ≥ attendance (derived) and computers ≥ need (lab default = attendance, per-scope overrides as requirement or preference); pins scoped/deliberate with DeliberateOverride conflict escape; catalog on the builder, unknown-room warn flag; placeholder ____ never assigned; no soft room rules (size-fit rejected); computer-need exception list cut to a mining research ticket.
- [Research: Mine computer-need exceptions](ScheduleLib-6xo.12, closed; docs/wayfinder/research/computer-need-exceptions.md): lab-default holds for 97%+ of 1,535 lab records (86 courses); declarations APPROVED (user, 2026-09-06): Mat. discr. 1 lab→0, Calcul variațional lab→0, PSI lab→0; reverse list (untyped-but-computer-dependent: Securitatea apl. web și mobile, Node.js server-side, ACI IT, Fotogrametria, RV&A, SMAI IT, Spring Security, Securitatea rețelelor, React, React Native, Producție virtuală 3D) → computer-need = attendance; MDL + Testarea jocurilor stay default (mixed evidence). Also user-confirmed: 423/4 carries VR headsets + 3D printer — first Room feature (flags participating in requirements).
## Not yet specified

- What the engine emits: how the solved schedule is written back out (existing Word/PDF pipeline? JSON?).
- Full-size performance target and what "good enough" convergence means on the whole university timetable.
- UNSAT/repair UX beyond solver mechanics: what the operator sees when requirements conflict.
- How the spec gets validated (review checklist? walkthrough against real data?) — settles during the grilling tickets.

## Out of scope

- Migration / minimal-change adjustment when late constraints arrive — later effort, after the solver is proven; depends on this map's output.
- Agent integration (email/Telegram constraint intake) — agents may drive the builder from outside, never the engine.
- Packaging, distribution, UI, notification emails.
- Full-production run on the entire university timetable (prototypes use a small real subset).

The room-rule semantics default a lab-type lesson's computer need to its attendance, with exceptions declared per course(+type) at builder level — but the exception list is unknown. Mine the schedule corpus (method as in docs/wayfinder/research/implicit-rules.md; room cross-tabs in docs/wayfinder/research/room-inventory.md) for lab-marked lessons that historically ran in rooms with no/low computer counts, and produce an explicit candidate exception list with evidence (counts, semesters), for the user to approve as builder seed declarations. title: Research: CP-SAT viability & timetabling modeling patterns
description:
## Question

Is OR-Tools CP-SAT the right tool and how is it used from C#? Nuget package + version for .NET (repo uses .NET 11 preview SDK), C# API patterns for timetabling (boolean lesson x day x slot x room variables, no-overlap via aggregate sum constraints, hard constraints vs weighted soft objective terms, AddExactlyOne etc.), determinism controls (num_workers, seed), expected performance on ~10^3-10^4 boolean variable problems, and a brief comparison against alternatives (Timefold/OptaPlanner, hand-rolled DFS) to confirm the choice.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text: RESOLVED. Full report: docs/wayfinder/research/cpsat-viability.md. Answers: (1) Google.OrTools 9.15.6755 (2026-01), net8.0+net462 TFMs, runtime satellites incl. linux-x64; runs forward-compatibly on the repo's .NET 11 preview SDK — pin version, smoke-test native load early. (2) Verified C# pattern: BoolVars per (lesson,day,slot[,room]), AddExactlyOne, aggregate sum<=1 no-overlap rows, co-timing via x[a]==x[b] per slot, weighted penalty terms into Minimize. (3) Determinism = num_search_workers:1 + random_seed + pinned version; avoid wall-clock cutoffs for reproducibility (max_deterministic_time instead). (4) Faculty-scale (~5e4 literals) = seconds to feasibility, seconds-to-minutes to optimal; long tail is proving the last 1-2%; no incremental interface — rebuild + hint previous solution (relevant to future migration effort). (5) Alternatives confirmed: Timefold has no .NET dist, MS has nothing, custom DFS loses on weighted soft objectives. CP-SAT stands.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text:
RESOLUTION — input contract and seeding design

Architecture and names
• ScheduleScenarioBuilder is the single mutable configuration boundary. ParsedScheduleScenarioAdapter, JsonScheduleScenarioReader, and handwritten C# configuration all configure it.
• Build produces immutable ScheduleScenario M. M is composed, not flat: TeacherDirectory, GroupDirectory, CourseCatalog, RoomCatalog, LessonDemand catalog, and RuleSet.
• Rule is the umbrella term; Requirement is a hard Rule and Preference is a soft Rule.
• ScheduleSolverOptions is operational and separate from the scenario. ScheduleSolver.Solve(scenario, options) returns ScheduleSolverResult, which links back to the scenario/options and carries Score, rule evaluations, and ScheduleSolution. ScheduleSolution holds generated placements against the source scenario and converts back to Core Schedule through CoreScheduleSolutionConverter.
• LessonDemand means fixed course/type/teacher/audience composition plus RequiredOccurrencesPerTwoWeeks. Placement means generated day/slot/parity/room.

Source seam
• Consume only the immutable post-Build Schedule in src/ScheduleLib/ScheduleLib.Core/Model/Schedule.cs, obtained after src/Features/Integration/Tasks/Initialization/ScheduleLoader.cs. Never consume mid-parse ScheduleBuilder state.
• One run explicitly selects one PeriodId. Consultations and OneTimeLessons are excluded; FR/dated scheduling is future scope.
• Normalize physical source representations using the semantics of AddOrMergeLesson in src/ScheduleLib/ScheduleLib.Core/Parsing/WordScheduleParser.cs and LessonBuilderHelper.Diff/Merge in src/ScheduleLib/ScheduleLib.Core/Model/Builders/LessonBuilder.cs. The all-teachers Excel formatter is presentation-only and must not define engine identity.
• Rows proven to be the same physical teaching activity may contribute multiple audience slices to one LessonDemand. Then aggregate identical composition across placements into RequiredOccurrencesPerTwoWeeks: OddWeek or EvenWeek contributes 1, EveryWeek contributes 2. Thus complementary odd+even becomes 2 and EveryWeek+OddWeek becomes 3. Day, slot, parity side, and room do not define demand identity.
• Parity in the initial generator is coverage quantity, not preservation: the solver chooses parity sides/splits under the 6xo.2 rules. Fresh generation receives no hint from the imported placement. Baseline-placement shape for future minimal-change solving is deliberately deferred.

Critical correction
• There is no co-timing/parallel-set requirement. Do not infer or model one from coincident source placements. Language partitions and lab/specialization meetings retain exact audience distributions and are otherwise independently placeable.
• Bloc is real Sinteză choice metadata only: each student chooses one course from the Bloc, so those audiences are mutually exclusive and overlap is allowed. Bloc does not force its lessons to the same day/slot. This supersedes the earlier charting/map and group-structure notes that called Bloc or split lessons parallel-timeslot constraints.

Current enrichment and validation
• For the first iteration, teacher assignment plus Sinteză composition/attendance facts are handwritten, academic-year-specific C# configuration. Group headline counts are not useful proxies for partitioned lesson attendance. Missing teacher or attendance configuration fails seeding; unknown configured course/language/audience/Bloc references, differing composition, inconsistent section totals, or subgroup sizes that do not sum also fail instead of silently preferring one source.
• Readable JSON is also included in the first iteration as an alternate builder-configuring source and test fixture format. JSON uses teacher/group names and readable partition fields, not numeric IDs. Names pass through the same configured remapping/canonicalization path as the main app, then the builder interns them to typed numeric IDs. The exact audience/partition API is owned by the 6xo.1 resolution.

Required domain prerequisite
• 6xo.1 now records the required redesign: extract teacher storage, name remapping/enrichment, lookup and name-to-ID interning from ScheduleBuilder into TeacherDirectoryBuilder -> immutable TeacherDirectory; Schedule references the directory rather than owning teachers. Persist/share mappings so a teacher keeps one ID across schedules. Apply/evaluate the analogous GroupDirectory extraction. This redesign precedes the engine input implementation.

Target implementation files/types
• Under the engine project selected by 6xo.1: Model/ScheduleScenario.cs (ScheduleScenario and component references), Model/LessonDemand.cs (LessonDemand/audience/biweekly coverage), Builders/ScheduleScenarioBuilder.cs, Rules/Rule.cs (Rule/Requirement/Preference), Solver/ScheduleSolver.cs (ScheduleSolverOptions, ScheduleSolver, ScheduleSolverResult), and Model/ScheduleSolution.cs.
• In src/Features/Integration/ScheduleEngine/: ParsedScheduleScenarioAdapter.cs, JsonScheduleScenarioReader.cs, and CoreScheduleSolutionConverter.cs.
• In src/ScheduleDefaults/ScheduleEngine/: academic-year-specific scenario enrichment/configuration. Final assembly roots follow 6xo.1, but these are the concrete type/file responsibilities.

Deferred extension
• ScheduleLib-6xo.13 covers trusted external DLL configuration/custom Rules outside this repository; readable JSON remains the non-executable data path.

description:
## Question

Given the inferred room inventory (see research ticket), define exact semantics for room assignment: default 'curs lessons go in large computer-less rooms'; overrides: (a) pin this lesson to this specific room, (b) this teacher/lesson-type prefers a computer room instead of a curs room, (c) vice versa — a lab lesson requiring a large room. comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text: Input landed: read docs/wayfinder/research/room-inventory.md (engine worktree) before grilling. It carries the room inventory, curs/lab classification with confidence, the Psihologie/Limba-străină exception findings, and an open-questions list for the user.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text:
Resolved by grilling (HITL, AntonC9018). Deliverable: agreed room-rule semantics. Glossary updated in the engine worktree (CONTEXT.md: Building, Room, Placeholder room, Room pin, Computer need).

**Room model.** Room = Building + RoomNumber + OptionalFloor (dumb wrapper structs, no domain behavior). Identity = (Building, Number); floor is derived data: leading digit of a 3-digit number (237/4 → floor 2), explicit prose (Mediacor "etajul I" → 1), or a per-building known default (2a → floor 1) — NO general no-floor default. Building codes: 4, 4a, 3, 2a (≡ 2Anexă, alias confirmed), c, Mediacor. No room kinds: each room carries approximate SeatCount and ComputerCount (counts over booleans; flag array reserved for genuinely boolean features later). "Lab room" = room with a high computer count; nothing else.

**Pipeline placement.** The parser's room-name service (updated in place) parses labels into structured rooms and owns a configurable remap/alias table (2374→237/4, 404→404/4, 145A/4→145a/4 case-fold, 326/6→326/4 — typo FIXED in the source workbook fr/2.xlsx, both worktrees, 2026-09-06; 2Anexă→2a). Parser never fails on a room string. The room catalog is an explicit schedule-builder input: known rooms + approximate counts, tier-seeded (113/4, 213a/4, 404/4 ≈ 80 seats; mid-size ≈ 50; small ≈ 40; labs ≈ 24 seats / ≈ 20 computers), refinable per room anytime. Unknown-room policy flag on the builder: warn by default, error on demand. Room validation is coded into the schedule for now; a comment notes the intended generalization to an extensible external validation mechanism.

**Hard requirements (uniform shape).** SeatCount ≥ Attendance — attendance derived from the lesson's group partition, overridable per lesson (derivation itself belongs to the input-pipeline ticket). ComputerCount ≥ ComputerNeed — zero by default; lab-type lessons default to their attendance; "curs needs more people" is about capacity, not computers. Overrides re-scope the need per course, course+type, teacher, or group — each declaration chooses its tier: requirement OR preference. The global lab default stays a requirement.

**Pins.** A pin is a scoped rule (selector: lesson composition, course, course+group, teacher, … — it declares its own scope). A pin negates both hard rules and is never questioned (deliberate — no violation warnings). Overlapping pins are an ERROR unless the more specific pin carries DeliberateOverride(true), which acknowledges the overlap and lets the specific pin win.

**Special rooms.** ____ is the placeholder room: not a real room, never solver-assigned, triggers no validation; a lesson carrying it is scheduled normally — time AND room — like any unpinned lesson. PE/online lessons have no Room at all (outside the room axis, ~5% of lessons). Off-site venues (Mediacor, annexes, building c) are ordinary catalog rooms, usually covered by pins.

**Soft rules.** None in v1: size-fit (wasted-seats penalty) rejected — keep it simple; stability ("don't shuffle rooms") noted only for the out-of-scope minimal-change effort. The engine re-assigns rooms freely on re-solve.

**Follow-up.** The computer-need exception list (courses whose labs need no computers) is unknown — cut as a new research ticket to mine from the schedules, then declare explicitly per course+type.

Supersedes the map Notes' "two kinds (curs/lab)" room bullet and the "curs lessons get large rooms" default: largeness now emerges from capacity, not kind.

title: Grilling: Constraint model & scoring
description:
## Question

How do requirements (hard) vs preferences (soft, weighted) become C# constraint classes, and how does each map onto CP-SAT? Cover: the constraint interface (is evaluation-as-score enough, or does CP-SAT make the old 'nudge the search' idea moot?), the initial constraint taxonomy (compressed lessons / no overloaded days / teacher unavailable at time X / schedule A matches schedule B / start not before 10:00 / co-timing of split parallel lessons (specializations, optionals, language partitions must land on the same day+slot) / room-type defaults+overrides), how preference scores normalize and aggregate into one global objective, and deterministic tie-breaking. Deliverable: agreed constraint interface + taxonomy + encoding rules.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text: RESOLVED (grilled with user, 2 rounds). Two tiers: Requirement = solver constraint; Preference = weighted objective term. REQUIREMENTS: teacher no-double-booking; student no-double-booking (per group partition); bloc co-timing (all courses of a bloc + all lab subgroups of a section share day+slot); room-kind rule with overrides (semantics in 6xo.3); teacher cannot-teach-at-X. PREFERENCES (weighted): prefers-not-at-X / prefers >=10:00 (per teacher); compressed days (students); student day-load hard cap 6/day + soft target <=5 (escalating penalty); teachers have NO day-load rule; PE (educatie fizica) preferably last lesson of day (soft, experimental — students skip after it); teacher-schedule-matching. PARITY SPLITS: weekly lesson = 1-2 placements, each with parity set {odd, even, both}, placements' parity sets disjoint (both-halves-odd allowed); no-overlap is parity-aware; per-split penalty (simpler schedules preferred). STRUCTURAL CONSTRAINTS: never typed in builder (auto-added, like gravity); architecture permits fully-external declarative encoding but core fast-paths expected — externality perf is a REQUIRED experiment on 6xo.6. SCORING: plain weighted sum, NO lexicographic hierarchy (user); 0-1 global score is report-only (objective/worst-case). NUDGE INTERFACE: dropped — constraint classes only encode; CP-SAT solution hints at solver-driver level replace steering (user accepted after deep-dive). DETERMINISM: dropped as requirement (user: speed first) — multi-worker, wall-clock budgets OK; reverses charting note. WEIGHTS: live at constraint-builder level (single place), NOT per-constraint-class constructor params (would duplicate); classes are weight-agnostic encoders. DEFAULT RULES+WEIGHTS: seeded from schedule-mining research 6xo.11; adoption decided by user here.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text: CLARIFICATION (user, post-close): parity splits are a SOLVER DECISION, not just input data — any regular lesson may split into odd/even halves during search. Consequence: 'audience has no splits' is unknowable at build time; per-parity gap counters (odd week + even week) are REQUIRED for every audience, always (the conditional-counter idea from the gap discussion is impossible, not merely wasteful). Encoding for the unsplit-preference: per lesson, placement booleans both/odd/even per (day,slot) with at-most-one-per-slot, odd side >=1, even side >=1, split => exactly two meetings total; isSplit[l] = 1 - sum(both[l,*,*]); objective += W_split * sum(isSplit). Odd+even halves in the same slot = a both placement (no special case). All split shapes (odd/even, odd/odd, even/even) cost the same single penalty. Open line for spec: confirm splits are at most TWO meetings per lesson.

comments.author: AntonC9018
comments.text: Terminology addendum from the input-pipeline grilling: Rule is the canonical umbrella term. A Requirement is a hard Rule whose violation makes a candidate infeasible; a Preference is a soft Rule whose satisfaction/violation contributes to the weighted objective. APIs and diagnostics may speak about Rules collectively, but must preserve this hard/soft distinction.
